user_goal: Browse the storefront and find products by category, with accurate category names, images, and product counts.
business_goal: Category browsing is a primary product-discovery path; stale or broken category pages directly cost sales.

edge_cases.case: A category just created in the admin panel does not yet appear on the homepage or its own storefront route
edge_cases.existing_validation: app/page.tsx and app/products/[categorySlug]/page.tsx both set `export const revalidate = 60` (ISR). There is no revalidate-on-demand webhook for categories — grep confirmed only "site-status" and "theme" tags have one (app/api/revalidate/), unlike nav-links which at least tags its fetch.
edge_cases.risk_note: This directly affects the admin-create -> storefront-visible flow: expect up to ~60s of staleness after creating/editing/deleting a category in the admin panel, with no way to force it sooner short of a redeploy. A test that checks storefront visibility immediately after an admin create should either wait out the window or explicitly assert the staleness rather than treat it as a bug.

edge_cases.existing_validation: Both getCategories() and getCategoryBySlug() catch ApiError and degrade gracefully — return [] and null respectively — rather than throwing or crashing the page.
edge_cases.risk_note: A transient failure during ISR revalidation silently degrades the homepage grid to CategoryGrid's own empty state ("Nothing to show right now" / "Categories are temporarily unavailable. Please check back shortly.") rather than preserving last-known-good data, if there was no prior successful cache (e.g. a cold start with the backend down).

edge_cases.case: Category route requested with a search query present: /products/[categorySlug]?q=term
edge_cases.existing_validation: The page redirects to /products?q=term BEFORE the category lookup / notFound() check runs.
edge_cases.risk_note: Consequence: /products/[a bogus slug]?q=foo redirects to the general search rather than 404ing, even though the category doesn't exist — this ordering is easy to get backwards in a test; assert the redirect, not a 404, when ?q= is present.

edge_cases.case: A category has no thumbnail_url uploaded in the admin panel
edge_cases.risk_note: mapCategory() falls back to a seeded https://picsum.photos/seed/{slug}/600/400 placeholder that looks like a real photo, not an obviously-broken image. A test asserting "an image renders" will falsely pass for a category that's actually missing its real thumbnail — assert the real image src/network request, not just image presence.

edge_cases.case: The general /products listing's own category-data caching window
edge_cases.risk_note: Could not be determined by static analysis alone — app/products/page.tsx has no revalidate export and reads searchParams (a request-time API), and cacheComponents is not enabled in next.config.ts. Whether getCategories() is cached there, and for how long, needs empirical verification (response timing/headers) during the live run rather than being assumed from hp-05/hp-06's plan text.

gaps: Whether any current header/mobile-nav link is configured to target a specific category (vs. just linking to /products generally) depends on live admin-managed nav-link data, not source code — verify live before writing alt-path tests around it.

This plan assumes categories only ever become storefront-visible via the ~60s ISR window (edge-01) since no revalidate webhook exists for them today — if one is added later, this plan and its test expectations go stale and should be regenerated.
/products page's exact category-fetch caching behavior (see the last edge_case) needs live verification, not assumption.
